title: Chapter 18 — Built-In & Integrated Refrigeration
intro: Built-in versus integrated versus columns, the engineering deltas, and panel-ready craft.

sections.title: The Three Levels of Built-In
sections.content:
Standard depth refrigerators sit flush with counters but are freestanding. Counter-depth is the affordable way to get the built-in look without the built-in price — typically 5-7 cubic feet less capacity than standard depth.

Built-in refrigerators are engineered to integrate into cabinetry. They are taller, have compressors on top instead of bottom, and accept custom panels. Sub-Zero, Thermador, Monogram, and JennAir are the major players.

Column refrigeration is the highest expression — separate full-height refrigerator and freezer columns, typically 24, 30, or 36 inches wide. Panel-ready, fully integrated, completely invisible behind cabinetry. Sub-Zero, Miele, Thermador, Gaggenau, and Liebherr lead this category.

sections.title: Engineering Differences That Matter
sections.content:
Sub-Zero's dual compressor system is the benchmark. The freezer and fridge run on separate sealed systems — freezer air never touches fresh food. Their air purification system, inspired by NASA technology, scrubs ethylene gas, bacteria, and viruses. This is not marketing — the food preservation difference is measurable.

Thermador Freedom columns use the Home Connect platform and offer the One-Two-Free program — buy qualifying appliances and get a free dishwasher.

Miele columns use their PerfectFresh system with independent temperature zones. Their build quality is exceptional — 20-year tested lifespan.

The customer at this level is making a 15-20 year decision. The engineering differences matter because they compound over that lifespan.

sections.title: Panel-Ready Installation
sections.content:
Panel-ready means the appliance accepts a custom cabinet panel on the front so it matches the surrounding cabinetry. The kitchen looks like furniture, not a showroom.

This requires coordination between the appliance retailer, the cabinetmaker, and the installer. The panel must be ordered separately. The hinge type, panel thickness, and handle placement all follow the manufacturer's specifications exactly.

Flag this at point of sale. The number one complaint on panel-ready deliveries is 'nobody told me I needed to order the panel separately.' Put it in writing on the quote. Confirm it at delivery scheduling. This one detail prevents a $500 return trip and a very unhappy customer.
